agree.reason: The calm tone and small, specific requests (an order confirmation, lobby notices, the assessment) are easy for a manager to grant, but nothing in the letter shakes her belief that only a few loud tenants are complaining.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the brief, and 'more than one day in every eight' holds for the year to mid-November; the only stretch is the softly inferred 'a day without getting to the doctor'.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the one-in-eight rate but never says that 74 of 112 households is two-thirds of the building, and never says that a part promised in six to eight weeks from June should have come by August, which is when the 12-day outage happened.

right_comparison.reason: The letter says that if nothing changes, the next outage will look like August, which is a fair picture of the status quo, but it doesn't use the five months of slipped promises to show things are not improving.

qualification.reason: It gives a checkable 30-day deadline for a reply and conditions the second-elevator request on what the assessment shows, but it never says what the association will do if the deadline or the delivery date is missed.

objections.reason: It deals well with the passing inspection certificate and the broken June promise, but it doesn't use the two-thirds petition figure against the 'few loud people' view she is most likely to hold.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted open letter of about 420 words, with clear headings, suitable for a lobby posting and a TV station.
